ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast; approximately 60% high-intensity (white) pixels located on the distal lobe regions versus 40% low-intensity (black) pixels concentrated near the peduncle and interior mottling.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant white contiguous fields on the left and right lobes. These regions are interrupted by a dense, heterogeneous distribution of small dark geometric blobs (mottling) and circular spots across the entire visible surface, with higher density near the lower-central junction.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 90 degrees.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations along the trailing edge with pixel-amplitude variations forming a jagged profile, particularly distinct on the inner-half of the lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave-to-convex upward trajectory from the median notch extending to the lateral tips, characteristic of a wide-spread fluke orientation.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple circular, high-contrast pixel clusters visible as dark spots on the white background of the right lobe and white spots on the dark trailing edges, consistent with barnacle attachment scars.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive clusters of barnacles (high-relief, calcified geometric protrusions) are visible on the extreme lateral tips of both lobes and scattered along the trailing edge.
other_distinctive_markers: Significant occlusion of the lower fluke and peduncle area by high-velocity water spray and droplets.
